issues.description: Silent behavior change: coerceNumber replaces toNumber, swallowing null as 0 instead of NaN propagation.
issues.detail: Original used toNumber directly, which returns null for non-numeric input, producing NaN math downstream. The new coerceNumber coerces null to 0, silently changing numeric semantics for panLinear/zoomLinear on bad input. This is a behavior change hidden inside a 'just added types' patch. State the change in the commit message or preserve the old NaN-propagation behavior.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the isNonEmpty guard runs inside pan/zoom.
issues.detail: panLog and zoomLog call Math.sign(domain[0]) before delegating to pan/zoom, so an empty domain reads undefined and yields sign=NaN before the error is thrown. The error still fires inside pan, but the order is sloppy and the new test only covers Linear. Either guard at the public entry points or add tests for Log/Pow/Symlog empty-domain paths.

issues.description: Local identity shadows the existing accessors.identity import that was used before.
issues.detail: The old file imported identity from './accessors.js'. The new file defines a local identity: TransformFn = x => x and drops the import. Functionally equivalent for numbers, but it diverges from the codebase voice and duplicates a utility that already exists. Either keep the import or justify the narrower-typed local in a comment.

issues.description: Domain parameter typed as number[] when NonEmptyArray<number> is what the code actually requires.
issues.detail: The whole point of isNonEmpty is to narrow inside, but the public signatures still accept number[]. A stricter type (NonEmptyArray<number>) would push the check to compile time for typed callers and make the runtime error a real backstop, not the only line of defense. Half-typed is worse than fully typed.

issues.description: peek overload pair is redundant since the second signature already covers the first.
issues.detail: function peek<T>(array: readonly [T, ...T[]]): T followed by function peek<T>(array: readonly T[]): T | undefined adds noise for callers who pass a generic T[] — they get T|undefined either way, and TS picks the non-empty overload only when the literal tuple type is known. Fine, but document why it's there or drop it.

review.summary: Patch does what it says on the tin: ports transform.js to TypeScript and adds an empty-domain guard. Diff is readable, scoped, and matches the rest of the vega-util typing work. One real concern: coerceNumber silently swaps toNumber's null-returning behavior for a 0-coercion, which is a runtime change buried in a "just types" PR — either own it in the commit message or revert it. Empty-domain guard lives inside pan/zoom, but the Log variants poke domain[0] first, and only Linear is tested. NEEDS-WORK: fix the toNumber semantics, broaden the empty-domain tests, and consider tightening the public Domain input type.
